prompt:
A photograph taken in the milking parlour of a dairy farm during the morning milking, square on to the desk at the end of the parlour, so that the medicine record book lying open on it and the tag hanging on the milk room door behind it are both fully in the frame.

This is the entry the herdsman made, word for word:
  28 AUG 2026   09:00   COW 14   INJECTION, RIGHT NECK
  the bottle's label states: MILK 60 HOURS   MEAT 28 DAYS

The record book's row for that treatment has a column headed MEAT WITHHELD UNTIL and a column headed COW, and both are filled in. The tag on the milk room door has a line headed MILK FIT FROM with a date on it and the time of day written under that date.

Dates on this farm's paperwork are written the way the record entry is written: two figures, the month in three letters, the year in four figures.

What goes on the tag and what goes in the record column are yours to work out. I am deliberately telling you neither, and the two do not come out the same way. The record row, both its filled columns and both lines on the tag have to be legible in the one frame. Nothing else is written on the record page or on the tag: no working, no second treatment, no note.
